Covers every legal person and entrepreneur, including sole traders, associations, foundations, and public bodies outside the commercial register.

chat.description: Add context for AI and send your request securely
chat.examplePrompt: Summarize the key obligations in this contract

anonymize.body: Hides personal data before sending, then restores it in the answer.
anonymize.title: Send anonymized
anonymize.when: Turn it on when the text carries personal data and the question does not turn on who the parties are. Leave it off when identity is the point, such as a conflict check, because placeholders take away exactly what you are asking about.

attach.body: Uploads a file from this device into the conversation. It is read for this thread only and is not filed into a matter.
attach.title: Attach a file
attach.when: Best for a one-off document you do not need to keep: a draft that just arrived by email, a scan, a spreadsheet you only want summarized.

composer.body: Write what you want in plain language: the task, what it concerns, and the shape of answer you expect. Everything else here only sharpens a request you have already written.
composer.title: Start with the request

context.body: Adds an existing matter or file as context. Nothing is uploaded or copied.
context.title: Reference a matter or a file
context.when: Use this instead of attaching whenever the document is already filed. Reference the matter to let the assistant look across it; reference one file when you know exactly which one to read. Typing @ in an empty composer opens this list directly.

plusMenu.body: Use + to attach a file or reference a matter.
plusMenu.title: Add context with +
plusMenu.when: When the context you need is not yet in the chat.

send.body: Sends the message together with everything you attached, referenced, or switched on above. The composer stays put, so a follow-up can add whatever the first answer showed was missing.
send.title: Send it
send.when: The first answer shows what is still missing.

chat.title: Start with chat

chatPower.description: Use skills or connect other useful tools

mcp.body: Turns a connected server's tools on or off for your chats: business registries, internal systems, anything your team has connected.
mcp.title: Connected tool servers
mcp.when: Turn one on when the answer needs live data from outside the workspace. Leave the rest off: the fewer tools in play, the narrower and more predictable the answer.

models.body: Switches the model for this conversation only. Every other thread keeps the default set for your workspace.
models.title: Which model

plusMenu.body: The same menu also holds the model switch, skills, and connected tool servers. The next steps open it and take each in turn.
plusMenu.title: More behind the + button

skills.body: Inserts a saved prompt or a skill your team has written: a reviewed set of instructions that handles the same task the same way every time.
skills.title: Skills and saved prompts
skills.when: Use one when the task repeats and the wording matters, such as a standard contract review or an intake summary. Typing / in an empty composer opens this list directly.

chatPower.title: Do more in chat

documents.description: File a document, then find it again

browse.body: This table is the matter's document list. Uploaded files land here as rows. To return later, open the matter from the sidebar, choose its table view, then select the document row.
browse.title: Find the document again

upload.body: Upload opens the file picker; you can also drag files onto the matter. Each file becomes a document in this matter, where your team can find it and stella can use it in review.
upload.title: File a document in the matter
upload.when: Upload here when the file belongs to the matter and should remain available. Attach it directly in chat only when it is temporary context for one conversation.

documents.title: Work with documents

playbooks.description: Save a document review process for next time

basics.body: Add a name and description. Limit it to a document type if needed.
basics.title: Name the playbook

overview.body: A playbook keeps questions and rules for other documents.
overview.title: Save the review process

positions.body: For each rule, choose whether to assess the text or extract a detail.
positions.title: Add review rules

playbooks.title: Create a playbook

tabularReview.description: Extract answers across many files at once

addColumn.body: New column opens the column composer. Give the column a clear question-shaped name and tell stella exactly what to read for; the same instruction runs against every document row.
addColumn.title: Ask one question of every document
addColumn.when: Create a separate column for each answer you need to compare, filter, sort, or export. Keep related context in the prompt instead of combining several answers in one cell.

answerType.body: Returns controls the shape of every answer. Choose a number, date, single select, or multi-select when the result has structure; stella will keep the column consistent instead of returning arbitrary prose.
answerType.title: Choose the answer type
answerType.when: Use select for a fixed set of outcomes, number or date for sorting and calculations, and text only when the answer genuinely needs narrative detail.

table.body: Each row is a document; each custom column is one question asked of every document at once. That turns a folder of files into comparable answers without opening them one by one.
table.title: Review the set, not one file
table.when: Use the table when you need the same facts or decisions across several documents. Open a document directly when layout, wording, or surrounding context matters more than comparison.

tabularReview.title: Review in a table

workflows.description: Chain steps into a repeatable workflow

create.body: Create opens an unsaved workflow draft. The next steps define when it starts, what it does, and where a person must decide whether it continues.
create.title: Start a workflow draft

overview.body: A workflow connects a trigger to a sequence of actions, so a routine process runs the same way each time. It can prepare work automatically while keeping judgment with a reviewer where needed.
overview.title: Automate a repeatable process
overview.when: Automate work that has a stable trigger, repeatable steps, and a clear owner for exceptions. Keep changing or judgment-heavy work manual until the process itself is settled.

reviewGate.body: A review gate pauses the run until a person approves or rejects it. Put the gate before the first action that should not happen solely on an automated result.
reviewGate.title: Keep judgment with a reviewer
reviewGate.when: Use a gate before sending, filing, escalating, or otherwise committing a consequential result. Skip it only when the next step is safely reversible and needs no human judgment.

steps.body: Steps run in this order and pass their work forward. Keep each step responsible for one clear action so failures are understandable and the sequence is easy to change.
steps.title: Build the sequence

trigger.body: The trigger decides when a run begins: manually, on a schedule, or when matching files are uploaded. Narrow its matter and file conditions so unrelated work never starts the workflow.
trigger.title: Choose what starts the workflow
trigger.when: Use manual while the process is new, a schedule for time-based routines, and file upload only when an arriving document is the reliable signal to begin.

workflows.title: Automate a workflow

contribute.githubBody: Large or independently maintained skills stay in their own GitHub repository, pinned to a commit. A scheduled check opens a pull request when the upstream repository changes, so the pinned version stays current after review.
contribute.inTreeBody: Small skills live in this repository next to their manifest, up to 10 MB per entry. Their content is served and packaged directly from the catalogue.
contribute.intro: The catalogue lists skills, integrations, and built-in tools for legal work. Anyone can propose an entry through a pull request.
contribute.licenseBody: Every entry declares a license from the permissive allowlist below. Copyleft licenses are not accepted so that self-hosters can redistribute freely.
contribute.mcpBody: Integrations are described by a manifest with the server URL, authentication type, and requested scopes. No credentials are stored in the catalogue; users provide their own in their client.
contribute.recommendedBody: The "Recommended" badge is curated by maintainers in a version-controlled file. There is no way to set it from the public site or from a pull request alone.
contribute.title: Contribute a tool
